InsightLandingPage.metaDescription: Not every business needs to start with a full-blown system. Sometimes the first step is just a page that puts an offer in front of the right people.
InsightLandingPage.heroIntro: Plenty of businesses have Instagram, WhatsApp, and word of mouth — but no page of their own that clearly explains what they offer and guides visitors to the next step.

index.umaPaginaUmaFuncao: A page doesn't have to do everything
index.quandoFazMaisSentido: When it makes more sense than a system

problema.title: Visibility isn't the same as having a page of your own
problema.paragraph1: An Instagram profile, a WhatsApp number, a referral from an existing client — that's visibility. It's not necessarily a place that explains the offer, shows what sets the service apart, and moves the visitor to the next step.
problema.paragraph2: Without a page like that, every interested person has to piece together on their own what the company does, from fragments scattered across different places.
problema.highlight: The problem is rarely a lack of visibility. It's usually not having anywhere to send people who are already interested.

siteVsComercial.headlineBefore: Having a website is one thing. Having a page built for a
siteVsComercial.body: A website presents the company. A commercial page moves someone to the next step: a form, a WhatsApp message, a quote request.

umaFuncaoSo.intro: It can do just one job, and do it clearly. Seen as a sales asset, the path is simple:
umaFuncaoSo.exampleIntro: A company that services air conditioners, for example, doesn't need a full system to get started. It can create a specific page: “AC maintenance for businesses.” There, the visitor finds:
umaFuncaoSo.closing: The goal is simple: turn interest into contact.

boaPagina.title: What a good page needs
communicatesItems: Proof or relevant information, when available
boaPagina.closing: None of this depends on a big website. It depends on the page being built with a goal in mind, not just to exist.

quandoFazSentido.title: When a page makes more sense than a system
quandoFazSentido.paragraph1: Not every problem calls for full software. A page can be enough when a company needs to announce something quickly, test an offer, capture leads, support a campaign, launch a new service, or validate an idea before investing in something bigger.
quandoFazSentido.paragraph2: When operations start demanding more complex processes, users, rules, and integrations, that's when the next step might be a system.
quandoFazSentido.stepsTitle: From first contact to the next step
quandoFazSentido.closing: Web development can be part of the sales process, not just a visual deliverable.

comecarPequeno.title: Starting small
comecarPequeno.intro: A company doesn't need to wait until its entire digital operation is ready to get started. It can start with a page.
comecarPequeno.closing: A website, automation, and software aren't separate choices. They're stages of the same path.

bigIdea.headlineAfter: and big in the job it does.
bigIdea.body: It puts an offer out into the world. It shortens the time between an idea and its launch. It starts capturing contacts before any system even exists.
bigIdea.finalLine: The first step doesn't need to be big. It needs to work.

conclusion.paragraph1: Maybe your business doesn't need a new system right now.
conclusion.paragraph2: Maybe it just needs a better way to present what it already sells.
conclusion.ctaTitle: Is there an offer your business hasn't put online yet?
conclusion.ctaBody: The next step can be simple: a page that presents what you already do, well.
